sections.content:
Population change in Watford in 2032

The population in Watford is projected to increase from 103,043 people in 2022 to 106,220 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 9,898 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Watford
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Watford, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 4,482, with 12,481 births and 7,998 deaths in Watford between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Watford by 4.4%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 9,898, with 78,452 people moving to the area and 88,350 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Watford by 9.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 692, with 1,344 people moving to the area and 2,036 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Watford by 0.7%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 9,225, with 18,912 people moving to the area and 9,687 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Watford by 9.0%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Watford in 2032

The median age in Watford is projected to rise from 37 years in 2022 to 38 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 14% of the population in Watford are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 12% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Watford between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Watford is projected to stay the same, at around 68%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 180 to 190 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Watford?

In 2032, 22% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 24% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Watford between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
